name: Comfort UI
author: Local UI Workshop
description:
Comfort UI 0.6.1 stable release: a configurable 13-language interface and in-game keyboard with local word suggestions, Chinese pinyin, Japanese romaji/common kanji, Korean Hangul composition, language switching and enabled/default keyboard settings. Desktop Windows IME/Win+H uses an embedded child of the game window, with no external input dialog. System IMEs/speech require appropriate Windows components; actual Cohtml/Win+H/VR compatibility still needs client testing.

Includes cumulative menu, scrolling/font, camera, microphone state/feedback, chat bubble, nameplate, animation and translation bridge fixes. Typed JSON events, explicit escaping, strict response/session checks and plain-text rendering are retained. Stable is the release channel, not a guarantee of bug-free operation.

[Installer](https://github.com/xuan5636/ChilloutVR-ComfortUI/releases/download/v0.6.1/ComfortUI-Setup-0.6.1.exe) | [Keyboard guide](https://github.com/xuan5636/ChilloutVR-ComfortUI/blob/v0.6.1/docs/KEYBOARD.md) | [Release/feedback](https://github.com/xuan5636/ChilloutVR-ComfortUI/releases/tag/v0.6.1)

Online translation remains opt-in and sends selected/visible text to the chosen service. Suggestions stay local. Word data has separate CC BY-SA/MIT/Apache notices. Unofficial mod, not affiliated with, approved, verified or supported by ChilloutVR or Alpha Blend Interactive. Modifications may affect performance, security or stability.
requirements: Windows x64 and .NET Framework 4.8; local model download is optional. See repository installation and translation documentation.
changelog: 0.6.1 hotfix: fixes startup failure that left all menus in the original UI when the game loaded its older Json.NET API. Both game/loader JSON binaries share identity but differ in overloads. Uses common writer calls, compiles against the game API and checks all JSON member references against both. Retains 0.6.0 native-layout multilingual keyboard. Actual game restart/IME/Win+H/VR remain to be tested.
